subject: Request: KV/log pruning retention waiver + DPA addendum coordination
messages:
From: Devon Smith <devon.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention exception for KV/cache audit logs

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Our compliance team is prepping an audit that will need a longer retention window for a small subset of operational logs (specifically kv-cache-audit.log and access.log for production region us-west-2) for 180 days instead of Redwood’s standard 90-day purge.

Two asks: can Redwood provide a documented exception path (playbook) that details how you implement a temporary retention waiver, where snapshots are held, and the rollback/secure-delete steps once the window closes? Second, we’ll need a short DPA addendum and an updated subprocessor attestation to reflect any escrow/backup subprocessors used for these longer-lived snapshots.

We’re timeboxed — audit kickoff is mid-June. Please let us know feasible timelines and what you need from procurement/legal.

— Devon
Compliance / Acme Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Devon Smith <devon.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention exception for KV/cache audit logs

Devon — thanks, this is clear and reasonable. High-level plan from Redwood:

1) Scope & isolation: we’ll create a retention waiver scoped to the specific log objects you list (kv-cache-audit.log, access.log) and limit retention to the named project + prod cluster in us-west-2. No customer request data will be retained beyond existing policies.

2) Implementation: we’ll take controlled snapshots (immutable GCS/S3 objects) of the logs daily, tag them with a retention-waiver label, and hold them in a restricted bucket with stricter ACLs for exactly 180 days. After the window we run the documented irreversible deletion playbook and attest to deletion.

3) Timeline: draft playbook + tech implementation plan by EOD 2027-05-31, DPA addendum draft to legal by 2027-06-01, DocuSign for signatures by 2027-06-03 to meet your mid-June timeline.

Attached: proposed_retention_waiver_playbook.pdf (high-level runbook). I’ve looped in Kimberly and Karthik for the purge mechanics and subprocessor attestation. Grace — can you confirm we can meet the DocuSign timeline and whether Marketplace partner Nimbus will be involved for any escrow snapshots?

Next step: Devon/procurement — confirm final list of log filenames and the account/project ids so we can scope policy.

Thanks,
Marcus
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention exception for KV/cache audit logs

Marcus — copying some implementation detail below (keeps steps aligned with playbook):

• Purge staging: we will create a separate purge queue for waiver-tagged objects so they do not flow into the standard 90-day deletion job. The deletion-job will consult the waiver label and skip until waiver expiry.
• Snapshot cadence & escrow: daily snapshots, incremental compression, stored in a restricted S3 path with server-side encryption (KMS-backed). If Nimbus Marketplace is used for storage, we’ll need to add them to the subprocessor list and provide an attestation.
• Forensic access: only authorized SecOps or an appointed Acme auditor can request exports; every access is logged and we’ll provide a scope-limited audit trail.

I’m attaching backup_purge_matrix_v2.xlsx — it maps log types to retention buckets, snapshot cadence, and deletion hooks.

One caveat: cross-border transfer rules — if any of the snapshots are replicated to a non-US region for durability, we need to run the DPA transfer clause and potentially an SCC/standard-transfer mechanism. Karthik, please flag if we need a data-transfer addendum.

Regards,
Kimberly
Head, Reliability Engineering
